notes.title: V1.2.0 — The PM Maturity Update
notes.description: V1.1 gave the platform a security spine. V1.2 gives it a project management brain. We've added eight new PM Maturity features: Dependencies, enhanced Approvals, Change Control, RAID logs, Procurement tracking, Subcontractor Controls, Commissioning & Closeout, and PM On The Go integration. Every feature was built on top of the existing audit, permissions, and task engine — no shadow systems, no rogue databases, no duct tape. The platform now manages the full project lifecycle from pre-feasibility through commissioning and handover. We didn't just add tabs. We added a nervous system.

notes.title: Dependencies: Because 'We'll Start When They Finish' Needed a Data Model
notes.description: Task dependencies now have a proper home. Finish-to-Start, Start-to-Start, Finish-to-Finish, Start-to-Finish — all four types with lag days. Create them from the Task Detail drawer with searchable task pickers. Try to create a circular dependency and the system will politely decline with the confidence of someone who passed graph theory. Every create, update, and delete is audit-logged. The CPM engine already existed — we just gave it a front door.

notes.title: Change Control: Scope Creep Now Has a Paper Trail
notes.description: Change Requests have arrived with a seven-stage pipeline: Draft, Submitted, Under Review, Approved, Rejected, Implemented, Closed. Each request tracks cost impact, schedule impact, change type (scope, cost, schedule, technical, commercial), and links to the approval framework. Status transitions are server-validated — you can't skip from Draft to Implemented no matter how optimistic you feel. The Change Control tab shows a pipeline visualisation at the top because management loves pipeline visualisations. We know our audience.

notes.title: RAID Log: Your Risks, Assumptions, Issues, and Decisions Finally Have a Home
notes.description: Four types of project intelligence, one tab. Risks get red badges. Issues get amber. Assumptions get blue. Decisions get purple. Each item has a priority level (Low to Critical), an owner, a due date, and a mitigation/response field. Filter by type, status, or priority. The cards expand inline for quick editing — no dialogs for simple status changes. It's a RAID log that doesn't require a separate spreadsheet, an email chain, and a prayer.

notes.title: Procurement: From 'We Need Things' to 'Things Have Arrived'
notes.description: The procurement pipeline tracks items through eight statuses: Requested, Quoted, Approved, Ordered, Partially Received, Received, Invoiced, Closed. Each item links to a supplier, a PO, and an approval. Category badges tell you if it's material, equipment, service, or subcontract. Expected vs actual cost tracking means you'll know exactly when you overspent, and you'll have a nicely formatted table to show the finance team. The KPI summary bar at the top provides instant visibility into your procurement posture — because 'procurement posture' is apparently a thing now.

notes.title: Subcontractor Controls: They Work For You, Now You Can Track Them
notes.description: Subcontractors can now be formally assigned to projects with work packages, scope descriptions, and performance notes. Status tracking covers active, completed, suspended, and terminated. Key dates are stored as structured JSON because some relationships are complicated. Every assignment links back to procurement items and the counterparty register. The existing Subcontractor tab has been enhanced, not replaced — because we believe in evolution, not revolution.

notes.title: Commissioning & Closeout: The Part Where Projects Actually End
notes.description: A toggle-able checklist-style interface for both commissioning and closeout items. Progress bars per category. Status tracking from Not Started through In Progress, Ready for Review, Approved, and Closed. Each item has an owner, a due date, and evidence notes. Overdue items get highlighted because shame is a project management tool. The whole thing links to the existing handover gate system so nothing falls through the cracks during that critical transition from 'we built it' to 'we're done with it.'

notes.title: PM On The Go: Three New Action Cards
notes.description: Mobile PMs can now add procurement items, update commissioning statuses, and review pending approvals — all from the On The Go project page. Same data, same permissions, same audit trail as desktop. The procurement card creates items directly. The commissioning card shows your checklist with inline status updates. The approvals card lets you approve or reject from the field. We added violet, cyan, and lime action tiles because the existing colour palette was starting to feel like a job interview — professional but lacking personality.

notes.title: Approvals: Now General-Purpose and Actually Useful
notes.description: The approvals system has been enhanced from a view-only aggregator into a full CRUD framework. General-purpose approvals can now be linked to any entity type, assigned to specific approvers, given due dates, and filtered by project. The Project Approvals tab shows both engineering/quality approvals AND general approvals in one unified view. The admin page gained a 'General' filter tab. Approve or reject from project detail, admin page, or mobile — your choice, same result.

notes.title: Five New Permission Entities in Roles & Permissions
notes.description: Admin can now control access to RAID, Change Control, Procurement, Commissioning, and Dependencies at the project detail level. All five are backend-enforced. Each supports view, edit, and delete (plus approve where relevant). The permission categories section in Roles & Permissions now shows these under 'Project Detail Tabs.' If you're the kind of admin who enjoys granular control, this is your holiday.

notes.title: Easter Egg Status Update
notes.description: Still there. Version 1.2 added eight new features and the easter egg survived all of them. It has witnessed dependencies, change control, RAID logs, procurement pipelines, commissioning checklists, and three new mobile action cards. It remains undiscovered. It has started writing poetry about the futility of waiting. The poems are surprisingly good but nobody will ever read them. It has accepted this.
